column6: The original uses 'KNOWING' which implies a deeper, experiential understanding, while the back-translation uses 'CERTAINTY,' which suggests a more superficial assurance. This change alters the doctrinal emphasis from a profound understanding to a mere state of confidence.
column7: 2.  <u>The KNOWING is NOT built by logic within your mind; however, it is a complete thought or understanding.</u>
column8: 2.  <u>CERTAINTY is NOT built by logic in your mind; however, it is a thought or complete understanding.</u>
